- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment shows strong bearish momentum (≥0.33) in last 3–5 days, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or weak; apply a 1–2% upward bias for first 7–10 days if sentiment < 0.67.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, add 1–2% per day if sentiment is bullish.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., 1.00 → 0.00) triggers a 2–3 day lag correction: forecast should drop 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is >0.75 for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to overfit recent trends; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid over-optimism.
